Whether a SELECTED citation's halo survives an editor remount/.tex re-parse. Editor regenerates citation ids on parse (useCitations.ts:352-374; syncFromEditor runs once per editor mount, EditorPane.tsx:1177-1182), so the sidecar gets fresh ids while cardStore.selected/selectedCitationId hold the OLD id. Code strongly implies the halo is lost + the selected-id is dangling, but confirming the reload sequence (does cardStore reset on remount?) needs a live reload step. A \cite atom embedded in a footnote/note card BODY (RichTextField editable, or BorrowedMainText read-only — both mount the Citation node-view via buildBorrowedAtomSchema) dispatches virgil-citation-click with the citationId persisted in THAT body's JSON. The main-doc citation observer regenerates ids on parse and rewrites the sidecar, but nested-body atom ids never re-sync, so detail.citationId drifts → setSelectedCitationId(staleId) selects no/ wrong card.

marker-clicks.ts:319-322 resolves the click sourceEl with document.querySelector('.citation-node[data-citation-id=...]') — the FIRST instance in the document, which for a nested-body click is typically the main-text instance, not the clicked one. alignOmniCardWithClick then aligns to the wrong source rect (clickY is right, sourceEl is wrong).

biblatex singular→plural auto-promote (CitationCard.tsx:375-388) has NO demote. After promote type='cites', reducing to one row (removeRow :392-402) or re-equalizing postnotes never resets type → serializeCiteCommand emits '\cites{key}' for a single key (bib-parser.ts:337-339 uses cmdBase verbatim) and the Type dropdown stays stuck on \cites. No package-migration of existing card commands.

setRowKey (CitationCard.tsx:361-368) / the picker do NOT dedup keys, so two rows can hold the same citekey → serializeCiteCommand emits a duplicate-key command (\citep{smith,smith}) and the header shows it twice. handleCardDrop dedups (:514) but the picker path does not — inconsistent.

findings.subject: citations
findings.symptom: A collapsed multi-key citation card (e.g. \cites{a,b,c,d}) renders one header line per key, growing several rows tall instead of staying compact like every other collapsed card.
findings.suspectedRootCause: The citation header bypasses the shared compressed-body line-clamp. CitationCard renders headerContent (which maps over ALL headerRowData rows) inside the compressed branch (CitationCard.tsx:751-752) with only overflowWrap:'anywhere' and no WebkitLineClamp / compressedBodyStyle ceiling — unlike EditableCard's compressed body (panel-primitives.tsx:1048-1076) which clamps to compressedLines.

evidence.note: compressed branch wraps the full multi-row headerContent in px-3 py-1.5 with no clamp
headerRowData.map renders a <div> per key — N rows tall when collapsed

reproSteps: Create a citation with 4+ keys (\cites{a,b,c,d}).
Collapse the card.
Observe the collapsed header is 4 lines tall, breaking the uniform single/clamped-line collapsed card rhythm.
findings.suspectedClass: Any bespoke card header that lists per-row content in its compressed view without routing through compressedBodyStyle — check the multi-paragraph report omni rows and any future multi-anchor card.

findings.subject: citations
findings.symptom: After the doc reloads / the editor re-parses the .tex, a previously-selected citation card loses its selection halo (and the panel's selectedCitationId points at an id that no longer exists).
findings.suspectedRootCause: The editor regenerates citation ids on every parse; syncFromEditor rewrites citations.json with the NEW ids (useCitations.ts:357-374) while cardStore.selected and the layout's selectedCitationId still hold the OLD id. Because citation is an inline-atom kind, the reconciler's pruner treats it as entityExists⇒true (useAnchorHighlightReconciler.ts:84-90) and never clears the dangling selection, so the halo silently mismatches.

evidence.note: syncFromEditor maps editor citations to fresh ids (id: ec.citationId), dropping prior anchored ids
syncFromEditor runs once per editor mount → ids rotate on remount/reparse
entityExists returns true for any inline-atom kind, so the pruner never clears a citation's stale cardStore.selected

reproSteps: Open a doc with \cite atoms.
Select a citation card (halo on).
Trigger a doc reload / editor remount.
Observe the halo is gone and selectedCitationId no longer matches any rendered card.
findings.suspectedClass: Footnotes share the inline-atom entityExists⇒true exemption and the same id-keyed selection — verify whether footnote selection survives the same remount. The deeper class: any selection keyed on an editor-regenerated id (omni pos cache, omniPinStore) is invalidated by a re-parse for both citation and footnote.

findings.subject: citations
findings.symptom: Clicking a citation that is nested inside a footnote/note card body selects no card (or the wrong one) instead of selecting that citation's card.
findings.suspectedRootCause: The nested citation atom's citationId is persisted in the host card's body JSON and is NEVER re-synced when the main-doc citation observer regenerates ids on parse (only top-level doc atoms feed getCitations()/syncFromEditor). The node-view dispatches virgil-citation-click with the stale body-JSON id (citation.ts:269-287); the bridge does setSelectedCitationId(detail.citationId) (marker-clicks.ts:284) against a sidecar that now holds different ids → mismatch.

evidence.note: node-view dispatches virgil-citation-click carrying node.attrs.citationId from the local (card-body) JSON
setSelectedCitationId(detail.citationId) — assumes the dispatched id matches a sidecar citation
allEditorCitations / citationPositionMap derive only from main-doc atoms (rev.citations), never from card-body editors

reproSteps: Put a \cite inside a footnote body, save.
Reload so the main-doc citation ids regenerate.
Expand the footnote card and click the nested citation.
Observe no citation card highlights (the dispatched id is stale relative to the rebuilt sidecar).
findings.suspectedClass: Same drift hits nested footnote markers (data-footnote-id) inside other card bodies; any inline-atom id stored in a sub-editor's JSON diverges from the main-doc/sidecar id space after a re-parse (id-regeneration class, lead #3).

findings.subject: citations
findings.symptom: Clicking a repeated citation (or one inside a card body) aligns the omni card to the wrong on-screen citation instance.
findings.suspectedRootCause: marker-clicks.ts resolves the alignment sourceEl with a document-wide querySelector for the FIRST '.citation-node[data-citation-id=...]', which is whichever instance appears first in DOM order — not the clicked one. The clicked element's true rect is available (clickY in the event detail), but the sourceEl handed to alignOmniCardWithClick can be a different instance.

evidence.note: document.querySelector('.citation-node[data-citation-id=...]') returns the first match, not the clicked node
the node-view already has the exact clicked dom element but only forwards clickY, not the element

reproSteps: Cite the same key twice in a doc (two \cite atoms, same id is NOT shared — but a repeated nested vs main instance reproduces).
Click the second/nested instance.
Observe the omni card aligns to the first instance's vertical position.
findings.suspectedClass: The parallel footnote handler (marker-clicks.ts:262-269) uses the same first-match querySelector for .footnote-marker — same wrong-instance alignment for repeated/nested footnote markers.

findings.subject: citations
findings.symptom: After adding a second key with a distinct page range and then removing it (or making the ranges equal again), the citation stays a plural \cites command for a single key and the Type dropdown is stuck on \cites.
findings.suspectedRootCause: The singular→plural promotion (setRowPostnote) is one-way: it sets type='cites' when rows≥2 with distinct postnotes, but no code path demotes back to the singular form when rows drop to 1 or postnotes re-equalize. removeRow re-persists with the unchanged plural type, and serializeCiteCommand emits the plural base verbatim for a single entry.

evidence.note: shouldPromote → setType(type+'s'); no inverse demote anywhere
removeRow persists with the closure's current (plural) type unchanged
serializeCiteCommand single-entry branch uses cmdBase ('cites') verbatim → \cites{key}

reproSteps: biblatex package; create \cite{a}.
Add a second key b and give a and b different +range postnotes → auto-promotes to \cites[..]{a}[..]{b}.
Remove row b.
Observe the command is now \cites{a} (plural, single key) and the Type select shows \cites.
findings.suspectedClass: Lead #4. Any one-way command-shape mutation driven by row count/postnote distinctness without a symmetric inverse — same pattern would bite a future biblatex shorthand auto-switch.

findings.subject: citations
findings.symptom: Switching the bibliography package (biblatex→natbib) leaves existing citation cards holding biblatex-only commands (e.g. \cites, \autocite), which then serialize unchanged and show an inconsistent Type dropdown.
findings.suspectedRootCause: Package switch only flips the shared bibPackage; it does not migrate per-card type. The Type <select value={type}> over the package-specific option list has no matching option for the now-invalid command, and the next persist serializes with the new package but the old (foreign) cmdBase.

evidence.note: <select value={type}> over `types` (natbib OR biblatex) — a biblatex-only `type` has no option after switch
types is package-derived but `type` state is not reconciled when bibPackage changes
serializeCiteCommand(natbib) still emits cmdBase verbatim → \cites under natbib

reproSteps: biblatex; create a \autocite or a 2-key \cites card.
Open the panel menu and switch Package to natbib.
Open the card's Type dropdown (shows no/incorrect selection) and/or edit a row.
Observe the persisted command is still a biblatex-only command under natbib.
findings.suspectedClass: Any per-card command shape that depends on the panel-wide bibPackage but is not re-derived when the package toggles — also affects the inline display formatter path for the same cards.

findings.subject: citations
findings.symptom: A citation card can end up with two rows holding the same citekey, producing a duplicate-key LaTeX command and a doubled header line.
findings.suspectedRootCause: setRowKey (picker commit path) writes the chosen key without checking the other rows, unlike handleCardDrop which dedups. So picking the same key on two rows persists \citep{k,k}.

evidence.note: setRowKey maps the key onto the target row with no cross-row dedup
handleCardDrop DOES dedup (prev.some(r => r.key === bibKey)) — inconsistent with the picker path

reproSteps: Open a citation card, add a second row.
Use the picker to set both rows to the same citekey.
Observe the serialized command repeats the key and the header lists it twice.
findings.suspectedClass: Inconsistent dedup invariants between the drag-merge path and the picker path — any multi-key editor that dedups on one entry route but not another.
